clue.text: Ran wild in captivity, causing dreadful loss of life

indicators.note: the shuffled letters of the first word go into the word for captivity

parts.note: a cage is a place of captivity

indicators.note: running wild suggests letters out of control, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An escaped animal ran amok and killed many people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns RAN into RNA, which goes 'in' CAGE to give CA-RNA-GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnage is wholesale slaughter, a massacre with great bloodshed.

clue.text: Risk not completing part of a church

indicators.note: the church word is left unfinished, losing its final letter

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar

explanation.surface: Gambling on leaving a church section unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completing' cuts the last letter L from CHANCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble or hazard; to risk something is to take a gamble with it.

clue.text: Scruffy dog follows student's charity procession

indicators.note: the word for dog comes after the procession word

parts.note: a rag is a British student fundraising parade
to dog is to follow, tag along

explanation.surface: A shabby hound trails behind a student fundraising parade.
explanation.walkthrough: A student rag is a British university charity event, often with a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy and disorganised; motley and shabby in appearance.

clue.text: To a shopper, oddly enough, it may indicate possession

indicators.note: odd arrangement means the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Telling a customer about some strange item that implies ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' rearranges TO A SHOPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark added with an s to show ownership, as in the cat's bowl.

clue.text: Follow directions and prosecute

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Obey instructions and take someone to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result; to follow on from something.

clue.text: Naval ship requiring quarantine?

definitions.meaning: an aircraft vessel that ferries planes across the ocean
someone who spreads infection without showing illness is isolated

explanation.surface: A warship arrives with a disease aboard and must be isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft vessel is so named, and so is a person transmitting a disease, who may need isolating.

clue.text: Stocking up time?

parts.note: seems to be about buying supplies, but is the season when stockings are hung up for presents

explanation.definitionFit: The festive season when children hang up stockings for gifts.

clue.text: Type of wine

definitions.meaning: an old printers' size of type, five and a half points
the deep red colour of wine, as in a red port style

explanation.surface: A sort of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An old printing size of type, and the rich red colour or style of port.

clue.text: Unfairness in the value of shares

parts.note: equity is the value of shares in a company

explanation.surface: Injustice in how a company's stock is valued.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustice or lack of fairness.

clue.text: Solitary eccentric, supporter of the monarchy

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd loner who backs the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges SOLITARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist who backs kings and queens.

clue.text: A short spell of hostile behaviour

definitions.text: A short spell of hostile behaviour

parts.words: A short spell of hostile behaviour
parts.note: reads as a brief bout of aggression, but 'short spell' means an abbreviated spelling: the word is a clipped form of a longer one meaning provocation

explanation.surface: A brief outbreak of aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is British slang, short for aggravation, so it literally is a shortened spelling of hostile behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for aggressive, troublemaking conduct, clipped from aggravation.

clue.text: Games pitch out in the garden

indicators.note: the throwing word sits outside, wrapping round the word for a set of games

parts.note: to shy is to pitch or throw
a rubber is a set of games, as in bridge or whist

explanation.surface: Somebody tosses a ball about while playing outdoors in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sports field beside 'Games', but it is the verb to throw; 'out' wraps the throw round the set of games.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted area of bushes forms part of a garden, so the word names such a garden feature.

clue.text: Drink cures heart trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and reordered

explanation.surface: A liqueur that remedies heart complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the ten letters of CURES and HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: A green or yellow French herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Excessive discipline for male elephant

definitions.meaning: military slang for pointless spit-and-polish routine
the term for an adult male of elephants, whales and cattle

explanation.surface: Too much regimentation imposed on a tusker.
explanation.walkthrough: In British army slang, this word means excessive drill and polishing of kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Army slang for fussy over-strict routine, and the standard term for an adult male elephant.

clue.text: Silly men

parts.note: looks like foolish people, but silly point and silly mid-on are close cricket fielding positions

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'silly' positions are fielders stationed very near the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket fielders placed close to the batsman.

clue.text: Spoils actions meant to rectify

indicators.note: putting things right suggests the letters must be reordered

explanation.surface: Measures intended to fix something only ruin it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rectify' rearranges ACTIONS and MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil something by pollution is to taint or contaminate it.

clue.text: Crash of train carrying elderly actor

indicators.note: the scrambled rail word holds the word for elderly
a crash wrecks things, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: elderly means aged

explanation.surface: A train crash with an old actor aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash of' turns TRAIN into TRIAN, which is 'carrying' AGED: TR-AGED-IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Watches and obeys

definitions.meaning: keeps to or complies with a rule

explanation.surface: Keeps an eye on things and follows the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Looks at closely; also keeps or abides by a law or custom.

clue.text: Don't lose that quiet shyness

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical notation for quiet
reserve is shyness or reticence

explanation.surface: Keep hold of that modest reticence.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep or maintain something rather than lose it.

clue.text: First-day cover?

parts.note: looks like a philatelic envelope, but means what one wears on the day of being born: nothing but skin

explanation.walkthrough: A first-day cover is a stamp collector's envelope postmarked on the stamp's first day of issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nakedness jokingly called the outfit one is born in.

clue.text: He attacked the Romans but turned tail at first

indicators.note: the word at comes first, before the rest
turned round, the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A warrior assaulted Rome yet fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges TAIL into TILA, with AT 'first'. 'turned tail' reads as fled.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth-century leader of the Huns, who invaded the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Mourn for George, King-Emperor, the night before

parts.note: GRI, Georgius Rex Imperator, was George V's royal cipher
eve is the evening before an event

explanation.surface: Grieving for a monarch on the eve of something.
explanation.walkthrough: GRI stood for George, King and Emperor (of India), on British pillar boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sorrow, lament a loss.

clue.text: Leisure facility

definitions.meaning: freedom from work, comfort and relaxation
skill or effortlessness in doing something

explanation.surface: A leisure centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxation or rest, and also effortlessness or deftness in performing a task.

clue.text: Fan of sickness benefit?

definitions.meaning: a hospital breathing machine helps the sick

explanation.surface: Someone keen on state payments for illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sickness benefit is a British state payment to people off work ill.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-circulating device, and also the respirator machine used in hospitals to aid patients' breathing.

clue.text: Doctor to buy one a drink

definitions.meaning: to give medical care to a patient

explanation.surface: A physician offers to stand someone a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To give medical care, and to pay for someone's refreshment.

clue.text: Musical for jazz enthusiasts?

definitions.meaning: the Lloyd Webber show based on T S Eliot's poems

explanation.surface: A stage show aimed at jazz lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber musical, and slang for jazz fans.

clue.text: Poor relatives prepared to do a variety of jobs

definitions.text: prepared to do a variety of jobs

indicators.note: letters in poor shape are rearranged

explanation.surface: Impoverished family members willing to take on any work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges RELATIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptable and multi-skilled, able to turn a hand to many tasks.

clue.text: Former French island Napoleon went into

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: A Corsican-born emperor is banished to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was banished to Elba and later St Helena.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment from one's country, the state Napoleon was sent into.

clue.text: Boards another's child

definitions.meaning: gets on, as with a bus: taken as two words, puts a foot on
a spouse's son from an earlier relationship

explanation.surface: Someone else's child gets on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as STEPS ON, the first sense is boarding a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A son of one's spouse by a previous partner is someone else's child by birth.

clue.text: After exam, tucked into a meal with a will

indicators.note: the eating word comes after the exam word

parts.note: an exam is a test
to tuck into a meal is to eat, here ate

explanation.surface: After a test, someone eagerly devoured their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' looks like 'enthusiastically' but means having made a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for a person who died having left a valid will.
